title: Arrest model v2: 2-DOF (pelvis translation + torso rotation), lateral/forward cases, tests
context: RideBelt is an open, safety-critical Hee-Lee Oss project: an optional rider-worn backup restraint (low hip belt + short tethers) that latches into an open seat anchor standard (RAS). ALL safety content is DRAFT and not for use until a credentialed engineer signs off at the MVP gate (GOVERNANCE.md). Never remove a DRAFT banner, never give instructions for wearing or attaching anything to a ride, never copy text from paid standards, and respect the patent design-arounds in docs/research/patentability-fto.md. docs/analysis/arrest_model.py is 1-DOF vertical only. It cannot show jackknifing, rotation of the upper body out of a hip belt, or lateral and forward loads, which drive the Shoulder Module and center-strap requirements.
objective: Add a 2-DOF (or planar multi-body) model: pelvis held by tethers plus torso pivoting at the hip, with lateral (Gy) and forward (Gx) pulse cases, measured pulses from data/accel/ when available, unit tests, and a results section in load-analysis.md.
acceptanceCriteria: v1 results reproduced within 5% when the rotational DOF is locked (regression test)
Every assumption (segment masses and inertias, stiffnesses) cited or flagged ASSUMPTION
Results written into docs/analysis/load-analysis.md as DRAFT, banner intact
Merged as DRAFT only; release requires MVP-gate Safety Engineer sign-off (GOVERNANCE.md)
